en: The image shows the back side of an old postcard printed in red and beige. On the left is a vertical column filled with dense handwritten text in a cursive script. The center and right side follow the classic divided‑back layout: the top has the printed heading "Carte postale" and multilingual labels for the Universal Postal Union. Below are printed words "SCHWEIZ. SUISSE. SVIZZERA." indicating Switzerland. In the upper‑right corner is a red Swiss postage imprint featuring the word "HELVETIA" and a value of 10, with a circular postmark that reads "CHATEAU D'OEX / GENEVE" and a date. The right side contains the address written in ink, including a line "28 Quai de Bethune" and the city "Paris", with "France" written below.
